tur36-14: The natural course of a lumbar disc herniation is usually good. The body can gradually clear the herniated disc material; the further the disc has pushed out or broken off, the more likely it is to regress on its own (in one review: 96% for detached fragments, 70% for extrusions and 41% for milder protrusions). Most people improve considerably within 4–6 months; in the few studies available, this improvement was generally maintained over 2–3 years of follow-up. In a US population study of 561 patients diagnosed with nerve root compression radiating to the arm (due to disc herniation or degenerative changes) in 1976–1990 and followed for about 5 years, 90% of patients, including those who had surgery, had no or only mild symptoms at the last check-up; a quarter of the patients had surgery during follow-up.
